name: ACI 318-19 — Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete, exposure categories F/S/W/C

source.table: Table 19.3.1.1 (exposure categories and classes) and Table 19.3.2.1 (requirements for concrete by exposure class)
source.verification_note: Indicative values for design exploration, reconstructed from secondary-source summaries of Chapter 19, NOT transcribed from a purchased copy of ACI 318-19. Strength values are converted from the code's native psi units to MPa (0.00689476 MPa/psi) and rounded to 1 decimal place, which is itself a source of imprecision. Check against the published standard before any structural use.

F0.description: Concrete not exposed to freezing-and-thawing cycles
F0.notes: Category 0 = 'not exposed'; no durability-driven limit applies by definition of the class, hence null rather than absent.

F1.description: Freezing-and-thawing exposure with limited exposure to water
F1.notes: min_strength_MPa converted from ACI's 4000 psi. min_air_pct intentionally omitted (not null): Table 19.3.3.3 sets the target air content by nominal maximum aggregate size, which was not confidently recalled here -- the engine will report UNKNOWN for this rule.

F2.description: Freezing-and-thawing exposure with frequent exposure to water
F2.notes: min_strength_MPa converted from ACI's 4500 psi. min_air_pct intentionally omitted (not null); see F1 note.

F3.description: Freezing-and-thawing exposure with frequent exposure to water and to deicing chemicals
F3.notes: min_strength_MPa converted from ACI's 5000 psi. min_air_pct intentionally omitted (not null); see F1 note.

S0.notes: Category 0 = 'exposure negligible'; no durability-driven limit applies by definition of the class, hence null rather than absent.

S1.notes: min_strength_MPa converted from ACI's 4000 psi. max_scm_fraction omitted: S1 also carries a cementitious-material-type requirement (e.g. Type II cement) that this schema does not model.

S2.notes: min_strength_MPa converted from ACI's 4500 psi. max_scm_fraction omitted, matching S1 -- Type V cement / SCM-blend requirements not modelled.

S3.notes: Same max_w_b/min_strength_MPa as S2: recollection is that S3's stricter requirement in ACI 318-19 is expressed through additional cementitious-material-type and calcium-chloride-admixture restrictions (Table 26.4.2.2(b)-style provisions), not a lower w/cm or higher f'c than S2 -- those additional provisions are out of this schema's scope and are not modelled (max_scm_fraction omitted for the same reason as S1/S2).

W0.description: In contact with water where low permeability to water is not required
W0.notes: Category 0 = 'not required'; no durability-driven limit applies by definition of the class, hence null rather than absent.

W1.description: In contact with water where low permeability to water is required
W1.notes: min_strength_MPa converted from ACI's 4000 psi. min_air_pct null: W is a permeability category, not a freeze/thaw category.

C0.description: Concrete dry or protected from moisture in service
C0.notes: Category 0 = 'protected from moisture'; no durability-driven w/cm or strength limit applies by definition of the class, hence null rather than absent. ACI also sets a max water-soluble chloride-ion content for this category, which this schema has no field for and does not model.

C1.description: Concrete exposed to moisture but not to an external source of chlorides
C1.notes: max_w_b and min_strength_MPa intentionally omitted (not null): it was not confidently recalled whether Table 19.3.2.1 states a numeric w/cm and f'c requirement for C1 or leaves it unstated (as several other 'intermediate' rows do) -- rather than guess which, this is left UNKNOWN. ACI also sets a max water-soluble chloride-ion content for this category, not modelled here.

C2.description: Concrete exposed to moisture and an external source of chlorides from deicing chemicals, salt, brackish water, seawater, or spray from these sources
C2.notes: min_strength_MPa converted from ACI's 5000 psi -- this is the most-cited, highest-confidence figure in this pack (ACI's strictest reinforced-concrete durability requirement). ACI also sets a max water-soluble chloride-ion content for this category, not modelled here.

notes: ACI 318-19 exposure categories F (freeze-thaw), S (sulfate), W (water permeability), C (corrosion protection) -- a genuinely different taxonomy from the EN XC/XD/XS/XF/XA classes, not a relabelling of them. Systematic omissions, not guesses: (1) min_air_pct is omitted (not null) for F1-F3 because ACI Table 19.3.3.3's target air content depends on nominal maximum aggregate size, mirroring the same omission in en206.json/bs8500.json for XF classes. (2) max_scm_fraction is omitted for every class: S1-S3's cementitious-material-type and SCM-blend restrictions (roughly Table 26.4.2.2(b)) are not modelled. (3) max_w_b/min_strength_MPa are omitted for C1 specifically because it was not confidently recalled whether the standard states a numeric requirement there. (4) The chloride-ion-content limits ACI sets for the C category are out of scope entirely -- this schema has no field for them. Strength values are psi->MPa conversions and carry their own rounding imprecision on top of the underlying sourcing uncertainty.
